acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It is completely free with no account required, no paywall, no limits, and no ads. Generate and check as many passwords as you like.

mainEntity.name: Are my passwords sent to a server?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Every password is created and analysed inside your own browser using the Web Crypto API. Nothing is transmitted, logged, or stored. Close the tab and it is gone.

mainEntity.name: How long should a password be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Aim for at least 16 characters, and 20 or more for important accounts. Length matters far more than swapping letters for symbols.
We measure entropy in bits (length times log₂ of the character pool). Around 80 bits or more is practically impossible to brute-force and is labelled 'Very strong'.

mainEntity.name: Can I choose which characters to include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. On the Generator page you can toggle uppercase, lowercase, digits, and symbols on or off. You can also exclude look-alike characters (e.g. 0/O, 1/l/I).

mainEntity.name: Does the Analyser store the passwords I check?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The Analyser runs entirely in your browser. Your input is never sent anywhere, and no data is stored or logged.

mainEntity.name: Is the password generator cryptographically secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We use the Web Crypto API's crypto.getRandomValues(), which is a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) backed by the operating system's entropy source.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a password manager?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not strictly, but we recommend one. Password managers make it easy to use unique, strong passwords for every account without remembering them all. We have a guide comparing free and paid options.

mainEntity.name: What are the worst passwords I should avoid?

acceptedAnswer.text: Avoid 'password', '123456', 'qwerty', 'admin', 'letmein', 'iloveyou', 'password1', 'abc123', 'monkey', 'master', and any family or pet names. These appear in nearly every breach. Our blog has a full list.
